articles.title: Holiday marketing hits inflection point in 2026: What brands need to know
articles.summary: As marketers begin shaping 2026 holiday campaigns, a central challenge has emerged around balancing emerging AI-powered tools with proven tactics like influencer and creator collaborations. Consumers are showing a push-pull dynamic: they're increasingly skeptical of heavily automated or AI-generated marketing content, questioning its authenticity and relevance, while still responding positively to creator-led campaigns that feel personal and trustworthy. This creates pressure for brands to avoid over-indexing on flashy AI applications purely for novelty's sake, since doing so risks alienating holiday shoppers who want genuine, relatable messaging during a high-spend season. At the same time, creator partnerships remain a reliable driver of engagement and conversion, giving brands a dependable channel even as the broader marketing landscape shifts toward more automated, data-driven approaches. The takeaway for marketing teams is that success in the 2026 holiday season will hinge on thoughtful integration rather than wholesale replacement—using AI to support efficiency and personalization behind the scenes while keeping human-driven creator content front and center in consumer-facing campaigns to maintain trust and authenticity.
articles.li_summary: Brands planning 2026 holiday campaigns face a growing tension between consumers' wariness of AI-driven marketing tactics and their continued trust in creator partnerships, forcing marketers to recalibrate their strategic mix.

articles.title: Snapchat shares insight into luxury shopping trends
articles.summary: Snapchat has released findings from a newly commissioned study examining how its user base engages with luxury brands and products. The headline finding shows that 84% of Snapchat users report that social media platforms make them feel more connected to the world of luxury goods, suggesting these apps are becoming a meaningful touchpoint for premium brand exposure rather than just casual browsing or entertainment destinations. This data point signals to marketers that platforms like Snapchat are increasingly viewed by their audiences as gateways into aspirational shopping categories traditionally reserved for in-store experiences or glossy print campaigns. For luxury brands evaluating where to allocate advertising budgets, this kind of consumer sentiment research offers justification for deeper investment in social-first campaigns targeting younger, digitally native shoppers who may not frequent traditional luxury retail channels but still desire connection to high-end products through their everyday social feeds and interactions.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat's new commissioned study found that 84% of its users feel social media platforms bring them closer to the luxury goods universe, highlighting the app's growing role in premium brand discovery.

articles.title: Meta launches messaging app for teens
articles.summary: Meta has introduced a new standalone app called Direct, aimed at giving teen users a separate space for Instagram direct messages instead of keeping that function bundled inside the main Instagram app. The move echoes an almost identical attempt Meta made in 2017, when it first tested a dedicated Direct messaging app before quietly dropping the idea. By spinning messaging out into its own product again, Meta appears to be revisiting that earlier strategy, likely betting that younger users prefer a lighter, chat-focused experience separate from Instagram's feed, Stories, and Reels. The app keeps the core DM experience intact, letting users send messages, photos, and other content just as they would through Instagram itself, but positions it as a standalone download rather than a feature buried inside a larger platform. For marketers and brands tracking youth engagement, this signals Meta's continued effort to court teen audiences through simplified, single-purpose apps, following similar moves by competitors building separate messaging-first products.
articles.li_summary: Meta has relaunched Direct, a standalone messaging app that splits Instagram DMs into their own platform, mirroring a nearly identical app the company briefly tried back in 2017.

articles.title: Pinterest shares its first Creators to Watch list
articles.summary: Pinterest has released its first-ever "Creators to Watch" list, naming 20 influencers from around the world identified as rising voices for 2027. The initiative marks a new effort by the platform to formally recognize creator talent likely to shape trends and engagement in the coming years, rather than focusing solely on current top performers. For brands and marketers, the list functions as an early scouting tool, offering a curated starting point for identifying creators who may deliver strong returns on partnership investment before they become mainstream picks. Since Pinterest has increasingly positioned itself as a discovery and inspiration platform for shopping and lifestyle content, the creators featured likely span categories such as fashion, home design, beauty, and DIY, aligning with the platform's core audience behavior. By publishing this list, Pinterest is also signaling its ambition to compete more directly with other platforms' creator economies, giving brands a reason to deepen their presence on Pinterest through early, strategic creator collaborations rather than waiting until these influencers reach broader recognition elsewhere.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest unveiled its inaugural "Creators to Watch" list, spotlighting 20 global influencers positioned for growth in 2027, giving brands early signals on which creators to prioritize for future partnerships.

articles.title: Snapchat will show more info on mutual friends
articles.summary: Snapchat is introducing a new opt-in privacy feature that reveals mutual friends between users right on their profile pages. Instead of having to guess or ask around about shared connections, users who choose to enable this setting will be able to see a visible list of friends they have in common with anyone they view. The feature is designed to make it easier to verify who someone is connected to before adding them, which could reduce friend requests from unfamiliar accounts and build more trust within the app's social graph. Because it requires users to actively opt in, Snapchat is framing this as a privacy-conscious update rather than a default change, giving people control over whether their mutual connections are shared publicly. The rollout reflects a broader trend among social apps to surface relationship context that helps users navigate who to trust and connect with, similar to mutual-friend features already common on platforms like Facebook and LinkedIn, though Snapchat has not detailed a specific release timeline.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat is rolling out an opt-in feature that lets users see a list of mutual friends displayed directly on another person's profile, making shared connections visible instantly.

articles.title: Meta expands content protection to Instagram
articles.summary: Meta announced it is bringing its existing Facebook content protection system to Instagram, giving creators on both platforms the same safeguards against unauthorized reposting of their work. The system relies on automatic detection technology that scans for matches to a creator's original content across the platform, then sends an alert when a repost is identified. This mirrors the tool Meta already uses on Facebook, where creators receive notifications if someone else shares their video or photo without permission, helping them track where their content is being redistributed and take action if needed. By extending this feature to Instagram, Meta is aiming to give creators more visibility and control over how their content spreads across its family of apps, addressing a long-standing concern among creators about losing credit or engagement when their posts are copied and reshared by other accounts without attribution.
articles.li_summary: Meta is extending its Facebook content protection tools to Instagram, using automatic detection to alert original creators whenever their videos or photos get reposted by other accounts.

articles.title: Holiday marketing hits inflection point in 2026: What brands need to know
articles.summary: As brands begin shaping their 2026 holiday marketing plans, a central challenge is emerging around consumer sentiment toward artificial intelligence versus established tactics like creator collaborations. Shoppers are increasingly exposed to AI-generated content, recommendations, and personalized experiences, yet many still gravitate toward relatable, human-driven marketing such as influencer and creator partnerships that feel more genuine. This creates friction for marketing teams trying to decide how heavily to lean into automated, AI-powered campaign elements versus investing in creator relationships that have historically driven trust and engagement during the critical holiday shopping season. The tension reflects a broader industry inflection point: brands can no longer treat AI adoption as a simple efficiency play, since consumers are scrutinizing how and where it's used, especially in content that touches on authenticity and emotional connection. At the same time, creator marketing remains a reliable performance driver, pushing companies to find hybrid approaches that use AI for scale and targeting while preserving the human touch consumers expect from holiday messaging and promotions.
articles.li_summary: Marketers heading into 2026 holiday campaigns face growing consumer tension between embracing AI-driven tools and valuing authentic creator partnerships, forcing brands to carefully balance innovation with trust-building strategies.

articles.title: How CeraVe’s ‘Dune’ deal takes the brand’s social-first playbook global
articles.summary: CeraVe has struck its first-ever movie tie-in, partnering with the upcoming "Dune" film to become the "Official Moisturizer of Arrakis" in the lead-up to the blockbuster's December 18 release. The L'Oréal-owned skincare brand, known for leaning heavily into social-first marketing and dermatologist-backed content, is using the sci-fi franchise's massive fanbase and cultural buzz to extend its reach beyond typical beauty audiences into entertainment and pop-culture conversations. By aligning with a desert-set franchise where skin protection and hydration are a natural fit, CeraVe is positioning itself at the intersection of film promotion and skincare relevance, aiming to capture attention from moviegoers and online communities already engaging with "Dune" content across TikTok, Instagram and other platforms. The partnership marks a shift for the brand, which has largely built its identity through viral social campaigns and influencer-driven storytelling, now testing how that same playbook can translate into a large-scale entertainment collaboration with global visibility tied to one of the year's biggest film releases.
articles.li_summary: CeraVe, the L'Oréal-owned skincare brand, signed its first-ever film partnership, becoming the "Official Moisturizer of Arrakis" tied to Warner Bros.' "Dune" sequel ahead of its December 18 theatrical release.

articles.title: Instagram launches iPhone Duo-native app
articles.summary: Instagram has rolled out a native app tailored for Apple's iPhone Duo, the company's foldable-style device with an expanded display. Rather than simply stretching the standard phone interface, this version introduces functions built specifically to take advantage of the bigger screen real estate, suggesting changes to how content, navigation, and possibly multitasking are laid out compared to the standard iPhone experience. The move signals Meta's early push to optimize its flagship app for Apple's newest hardware form factor as foldable and dual-screen-style devices gain traction in the market. For marketers and brands active on Instagram, this could mean new creative possibilities on larger canvases, different engagement patterns from users on bigger screens, and a need to reconsider how ads, Stories, and Reels render on this expanded format. While specific feature details beyond the larger-screen optimization weren't outlined, the launch points to Instagram positioning itself early for a new category of Apple devices rather than waiting for broader adoption before adapting its app experience.
articles.li_summary: Instagram released a version of its app built specifically for Apple's iPhone Duo, adding interface functions designed to make full use of the device's larger foldable screen.

articles.title: X tests adding professional histories to user profiles
articles.summary: X appears to be experimenting with a work experience section for user profiles, allowing people to list past roles, employers, and career details directly on their X pages. The feature mirrors the platform's prior attempt at building a jobs-focused product, X Jobs, which debuted around two years ago but failed to gain significant traction or compete meaningfully with established players in professional networking. By resurfacing a work-history element now, X signals continued interest in expanding beyond its core social feed into career-oriented territory, potentially positioning itself as a rival to LinkedIn for professional branding and networking. For marketers and brand teams, this could eventually open new avenues for talent showcasing, employer branding, and recruitment-adjacent content directly within X's ecosystem, though it remains unclear whether the test will be rolled out broadly or quietly shelved like its predecessor. No details have been confirmed yet regarding timing, availability, or how deeply the feature will integrate with existing profile formats and verification systems.
articles.li_summary: X is testing a new profile feature that displays users' professional work history, echoing the platform's earlier X Jobs initiative launched roughly two years ago.

articles.title: LinkedIn adds monetization tab to profile analytics
articles.summary: LinkedIn has rolled out a new monetization tab within its profile analytics section, designed specifically for users enrolled in or eligible for the platform's Creator Marketplace. The addition consolidates data on profile performance alongside visibility into available brand partnership and collaboration opportunities, removing the need for creators to navigate away from their profile to check eligibility or track engagement tied to monetization. By surfacing this information directly in analytics, LinkedIn is making it easier for creators to understand how their content performance connects to potential paid opportunities on the platform. The move reflects LinkedIn's ongoing push to build out creator-focused tools and compete with other social platforms that have invested heavily in monetization features, such as TikTok and YouTube. For marketers and brands, this update could mean more creators actively tracking and seeking partnership opportunities, potentially increasing the pool of professionals available for sponsored content and collaboration campaigns through LinkedIn's marketplace infrastructure.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn added a dedicated monetization tab to profile analytics, giving creators direct access to Creator Marketplace opportunities and performance data without leaving their profile dashboard.

articles.title: Instagram adds Amazon affiliate links
articles.summary: Instagram has rolled out a new creator monetization feature through a partnership with Amazon, allowing users to tag shoppable products directly within their content and earn affiliate commissions on resulting sales. Creators can attach up to 30 product tags to a single Reel, while static feed posts are capped at 20 tags each. The integration pulls products straight from Amazon's catalog, letting followers browse and purchase items without leaving the Instagram app, streamlining the path from content discovery to checkout. This move deepens Instagram's push into social commerce, giving creators a built-in incentive to recommend products they use or endorse while tying that activity to measurable revenue through Amazon's affiliate structure. For marketers and brands, the update signals growing overlap between influencer content and e-commerce infrastructure, as platforms compete to keep shopping activity native to their apps rather than routing users externally. The feature expands Instagram's existing shopping tools and positions Amazon's massive product inventory as a direct extension of creator storefronts on the platform.
articles.li_summary: Instagram has partnered with Amazon to let creators embed shoppable affiliate product links directly in posts, capping tags at 30 per Reel and 20 per feed post.

articles.title: How AI and social media are changing the media mix
articles.summary: New research examines how artificial intelligence and social media platforms are altering the traditional path to purchase for consumers. Rather than following a linear journey from awareness to purchase, buyers are now engaging with AI-powered search tools, chatbots, and social platforms at multiple touchpoints before making decisions, blending discovery, research, and transaction into overlapping stages. This shift means marketers can no longer rely on conventional channel allocations or attribution models that assume a predictable sequence of steps. Social media in particular is functioning less as a top-of-funnel awareness tool and more as a direct commerce and research destination, while AI tools are increasingly inserting themselves into the comparison and decision-making process. For marketing professionals, the implications center on media mix planning: budgets and messaging strategies built around older customer-journey assumptions risk missing where consumers actually spend time and make choices now, requiring renewed investment in understanding how AI and social intersect with purchase behavior.
articles.li_summary: New research highlights how artificial intelligence tools and social media platforms are increasingly influencing consumer purchase journeys, reshaping which channels marketers must prioritize across the modern media mix.

articles.title: LinkedIn says influential voices are critical for AI chatbot citations
articles.summary: Robert Yanik, who leads AI search marketing for LinkedIn Ads, argues that large language models are fundamentally designed to reward credibility signals when generating responses, meaning brands hoping to appear in AI chatbot answers need recognizable, trusted voices behind their content rather than generic corporate messaging. As tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI Overviews increasingly shape how professionals discover information, Yanik's point is that these systems favor sources already carrying authority and engagement online, such as executives, subject-matter experts and established thought leaders, over anonymous brand accounts. For marketers, this reframes the optimization challenge: instead of only chasing traditional SEO rankings, companies now need to build and showcase influential individual voices whose expertise and track record signal trustworthiness to AI models. articles.li_summary: LinkedIn Ads' AI search marketing lead Robert Yanik says generative AI chatbots prioritize content from credible, influential voices when deciding what sources to cite in their answers.

articles.title: TikTok UK publishes live shopping report
articles.summary: TikTok UK has published a new report focused on its live shopping feature, highlighting a notable link between live-streamed content and offline purchasing behavior. According to the platform's findings, almost one-third of users who watch live shopping streams end up buying the showcased product in-store rather than completing the purchase directly through the app. This data suggests that TikTok's live shopping format is influencing consumer behavior beyond the platform itself, functioning as a discovery and consideration tool that drives foot traffic and in-person sales for brands and retailers. For marketers, this signals that live shopping campaigns on TikTok shouldn't be measured solely by in-app conversion metrics, since a significant share of purchase intent translates into real-world store visits. The report positions TikTok as a growing influence on the broader retail funnel, reinforcing the platform's push to be seen as a serious commerce channel rather than just an entertainment or discovery app for younger audiences.
articles.li_summary: TikTok UK released a live shopping report revealing that nearly one-third of viewers who watch live shopping streams eventually purchase the featured product in a physical store.

articles.title: Facebook shelves additional profile option
articles.summary: Facebook is shutting down the multiple-profile feature it rolled out in 2023, which had allowed users to create and manage separate personas tied to a single account. The company confirmed that any extra profiles users set up under this feature will be permanently deleted by mid-December. The feature had let people maintain distinct identities for different interests or audiences without creating entirely separate Facebook accounts, similar to how some other platforms support multiple personas under one login. No replacement feature or alternative has been detailed alongside the sunset announcement. Users who relied on these secondary profiles for niche communities, hobbies, or professional branding separate from their main identity will need to find another way to manage that separation, or consolidate that activity back into their primary profile before the deletion deadline hits. The move scales back one of Facebook's identity-management experiments just two years after its introduction.
articles.li_summary: Facebook is discontinuing its multiple-profile feature, introduced in 2023, and will delete all additional personas users created by mid-December.

articles.title: Meta begins internal tests of prediction markets app
articles.summary: Meta has started internal testing of a new prediction markets app, according to reporting from the Wall Street Journal. The app is designed to replicate the core functionality of established prediction market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket, allowing users to forecast and bet on outcomes of real-world events such as elections, sports, or economic indicators. However, a key difference from those platforms is that Meta's version will not involve actual cash transactions, suggesting the company is pursuing a play-money or points-based model rather than real-dollar wagering. Details on the specific mechanics, launch timeline, or which Meta platforms (Facebook, Instagram, or a standalone app) might host this feature have not been disclosed. The move signals Meta's interest in the fast-growing prediction markets space, which has gained significant traction and regulatory attention in the US, without the company wading into the legal and compliance complexities tied to real-money betting that platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket currently navigate.
articles.li_summary: Meta is internally testing a prediction markets app that mirrors Kalshi and Polymarket's functionality but excludes real-money cash transactions, according to a Wall Street Journal report.

articles.title: LinkedIn cracks down on AI-generated comments
articles.summary: LinkedIn has announced a fresh crackdown targeting AI-generated comments appearing across its platform, marking the latest step in an ongoing effort to combat what the company and critics call "AI slop" — low-effort, often repetitive content produced by bots or automated tools rather than genuine human engagement. The move reflects growing concern that comment sections, a key part of LinkedIn's professional networking and engagement model, are becoming flooded with generic, templated responses generated by AI tools designed to boost visibility or mimic authentic interaction. By addressing AI-generated comments specifically, LinkedIn is expanding its content-quality enforcement beyond posts and articles to the conversational layer of the platform, where authenticity has traditionally been a selling point for professional networking. This follows a broader industry-wide reckoning with AI-generated content polluting social feeds, as platforms from LinkedIn to others grapple with distinguishing genuine human voices from automated outputs. For marketers and professionals relying on LinkedIn for authentic engagement, this signals tighter scrutiny ahead on how comments are generated, posted, and potentially flagged or removed.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn is rolling out new measures to detect and limit AI-generated comments on its platform, continuing its broader effort to curb low-quality, automated "AI slop" content from cluttering user feeds.

articles.title: Sociable: Meta’s AI ads included unapproved discounts
articles.summary: Recent reports have revealed a flaw in Meta's artificial intelligence-powered advertising tools, which were found to display discount offers to customers even after businesses had disabled promotions. This means advertisers who intentionally turned off discount campaigns still had unapproved deals surfaced to shoppers, potentially undercutting pricing strategies and creating confusion or mistrust among customers expecting accurate offers. The issue highlights growing concerns around the reliability of AI-driven automation in advertising, particularly as platforms like Meta push businesses toward increasingly automated, AI-managed ad campaigns that offer less manual oversight. For marketers, this raises questions about how much control they actually retain when using AI ad tools, especially regarding pricing and promotional messaging that directly affects revenue and brand consistency. The report adds to a broader pattern of scrutiny facing AI-powered ad platforms, as advertisers weigh the efficiency gains of automation against risks of errors that can affect customer experience, pricing integrity, and trust. It remains unclear how widespread the issue was or what corrective steps Meta has taken.
articles.li_summary: Meta's AI-driven ad tools reportedly displayed discount offers to customers even when businesses had explicitly turned promotions off, raising concerns about advertiser control and trust in automated ad systems.

articles.title: How Unilever’s social-first marketing is evolving amid reorganization
articles.summary: Unilever has shared new details about how its marketing approach is shifting as it rolls out a broader company reorganization built on the principle of "global strategy, local execution." The consumer goods giant is restructuring so that overarching brand and marketing strategy is set centrally, while individual markets retain control over how campaigns are executed on the ground, including social media content. This shift reflects Unilever's continued push toward social-first marketing, where platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube shape campaign planning from the outset rather than serving as an afterthought to traditional advertising. The reorganization is designed to let global teams maintain consistent brand positioning and efficiency across Unilever's portfolio, while giving regional and local marketers flexibility to adapt content, tone, and platform choices to local audiences and cultural nuances. For marketers watching Unilever, long seen as a bellwether for large-scale brand strategy, the changes signal a broader industry trend toward balancing centralized strategic control with decentralized, locally responsive social execution.
articles.li_summary: Unilever detailed how its social-first marketing strategy is adapting as the company restructures internally around a new "global strategy, local execution" operating principle.

articles.title: Edits app gets speed curves and auto audio balancing
articles.summary: Instagram's video editing tool, Edits, has rolled out two new features aimed at giving creators more precise control over their content: speed curves and automatic audio balancing. The speed curve tool allows users to adjust playback speed at different points within a single clip, rather than applying one uniform speed throughout, enabling smoother transitions between slow-motion and fast-forward effects for more dynamic storytelling. The automatic audio balancing feature addresses a common editing headache by evening out volume levels across multiple clips or audio tracks within a project, reducing the need for manual tweaking to fix jarring loudness differences when stitching together footage from different sources. Together, these updates are designed to streamline the editing workflow directly within the app, cutting down on the time creators spend fine-tuning pacing and sound quality before publishing. The changes reflect Instagram's ongoing push to make Edits a more competitive standalone tool for short-form video creators who might otherwise rely on third-party editing software for similar functionality.
articles.li_summary: Instagram's Edits app added speed curve controls for variable playback speed and automatic audio balancing, giving creators finer control over pacing and consistent sound levels across clips without manual adjustments.

While details remain limited, the move suggests Meta is exploring ways to let users follow live games, scores, or sports-related content more directly inside Instagram rather than relying on third-party apps or separate sports platforms. This would mark an expansion of Instagram's efforts to keep users engaged with real-time, interest-based content beyond its core photo and video sharing functions, following similar moves by competitors to integrate live sports updates and fan interaction tools. For marketers and brands, a dedicated sports hub could open new opportunities for timely engagement, targeted advertising around major sporting events, and partnerships tied to live audience spikes. As with most early-stage app experiments, it's unclear whether this feature will roll out broadly, remain limited to select markets, or get scrapped before public release, but it signals Instagram's continued interest in tapping into sports fandom as a growth and retention lever.

articles.title: LinkedIn launches CTV ads in the UK

The platform states that its CTV ad placements are 2.6 times more effective at reaching genuine B2B audiences compared with other connected TV advertising solutions currently available, positioning the format as a differentiated option for brands focused on reaching business decision-makers rather than general consumers. This move follows a broader industry trend of advertising platforms pushing further into CTV as viewing habits shift away from traditional linear television toward streaming services, and it signals LinkedIn's intent to capture advertising budgets that might otherwise go to video-first platforms. For marketing professionals running account-based or B2B campaigns, the launch offers an additional channel to extend brand reach beyond LinkedIn's native feed, potentially allowing for more integrated, cross-screen targeting strategies that combine professional data with the high-impact format of television advertising.

articles.title: LinkedIn tests frequent viewer feature
articles.summary: LinkedIn appears to be piloting an expanded version of its profile-viewing analytics tool, according to a Wired report. Currently, Premium subscribers can already see a list of users who have viewed their profile, a feature often used for networking and sales prospecting. The platform is now testing an enhancement that would show the frequency of these visits, letting users know if someone has checked their profile once or returned multiple times. This added layer of detail could help professionals gauge genuine interest from recruiters, potential clients, or business contacts, distinguishing a casual glance from repeated attention. The feature is still in testing and has not been confirmed for a full rollout, so specifics on availability, timing, or whether it will remain exclusive to Premium accounts are not yet clear. If launched, this could further differentiate LinkedIn's paid tier by offering deeper engagement insights, reinforcing the value proposition of Premium subscriptions for users focused on relationship-building and visibility tracking on the platform.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn is testing a new feature for Premium subscribers that reveals not just who viewed their profile, but how frequently specific viewers have returned to check it out, Wired reports.

articles.title: X experiments with expanded AI transparency labels
articles.summary: X is testing a new automated system designed to identify and label posts that appear to have been created using artificial intelligence tools, marking an expansion of the platform's existing transparency features around synthetic content. Rather than relying solely on users to voluntarily disclose when they've used AI to generate text, images, or video, this experimental feature would allow X's systems to detect likely AI-generated material and apply a label automatically, flagging it for viewers. The move reflects growing pressure on social platforms to address the spread of AI-generated content, including deepfakes and synthetic media, which has raised concerns about misinformation and authenticity across the internet. By building automated detection into its labeling system, X aims to catch content that might otherwise go unmarked, giving users more context about what they're seeing in their feeds. Details on the specific detection methods, accuracy rates, or rollout timeline have not been fully disclosed, as the feature remains in a testing phase, but it signals X's continued investment in content moderation tools tied to AI-era challenges.
articles.li_summary: X is piloting an automated detection system that scans posts for signs of AI generation and applies transparency labels, expanding its existing content-authenticity tools without manual user disclosure required.

articles.title: Meta publishes explainer on Your Algorithm controls
articles.summary: Meta has published new guidance detailing how its "Your Algorithm" feature works, giving users more visibility and control over the content ranking system behind their feeds. The tool allows people to opt in or out of particular topics they do or don't want surfaced, effectively letting them steer what the recommendation engine prioritizes rather than relying solely on automated signals like past engagement. According to the explainer, this customization applies across personal preferences, meaning users can fine-tune their experience based on interests, sensitivities, or topics they'd rather avoid seeing altogether. The move is part of Meta's broader push toward transparency around algorithmic feed curation, responding to ongoing scrutiny over how social platforms decide what content reaches users. For marketers and brands, this signals that audience reach could become more dependent on user-selected topic preferences rather than purely engagement-driven distribution, making it worth monitoring how opt-in and opt-out behavior shapes organic visibility going forward across Meta's family of apps.
articles.li_summary: Meta released a detailed explainer on its "Your Algorithm" controls, letting users opt in or out of specific content topics to personalize how their feeds are ranked across its apps.
